items.content:
Despite balance sheet reduction, the Bank of Japan remains the dominant force in Japan’s bond market:

The Bank of Japan now holds ~46% of Japanese government bonds (JGBs), down -8 percentage points from its 2023 peak and its lowest proportion since 2021.

Yet, the BoJ still holds more JGBs than banks, life insurers, pension funds, and foreign investors combined.

By comparison, the BoJ owned just ~10% of JGBs in 2013.

This comes despite BoJ holdings of JGBs dropping -$310 billion over the 12 months ending in July, their largest 12-month decline in history.

This brought the BoJ’s total JGB holdings down to ~$3.3 trillion, its lowest since 2020, but still +400% above 2012 levels.

The BoJ is stepping back, but it still controls Japan’s bond market.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Sep 9, 2026

items.title: US tech profitability is exploding higher: Profit margins for Technology, Media, & Telecom (TMT) stocks are up to a record 24%. Margins have doubled since the 2022 bear market. Tech profit margins are now nearly 10 percentage points above their historic trend, which is currently running at ~15%. By comparison, profit margins for companies excluding tech stand at ~9%, in-line with their long-term trend. This is still below the 2007 peak before the Financial Crisis started and below the 2021 high. As a result, tech profit margins are now ~2.7x higher than the rest of the market. The AI Revolution is transforming tech's profitability.
